name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+30 partisan lean in a deep-blue Maryland district
Raskin's massive financial advantage ($7.9M on hand vs ~$1.8K)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no serious outside spending against him
model.rationale: Raskin holds a D+30 district with a huge fundraising edge and no meaningful opposition spending, and markets price him near certain. The fundamentals support a Safe D rating with a margin around 30 points.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge against Raskin would be the only plausible source of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jamie Raskin is seeking re-election in a Maryland district that leans Democratic by about 30 points, one of the most Democratic seats in the country. He has raised more than $7.4 million and holds nearly $7.9 million on hand, while Republican challenger Cheryl Riley has raised under $17,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Raskin roughly a 98% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
